scope: Three additional requested Analysis reports: Emanuel Milman, Mariusz Mirek and Joaquim Ortega-Cerda. Six Analysis reports are now registered; this is not complete coverage of the section.

mathematicalReview.scope: The coordinator read every new atomic note, all three overviews and references, and all three source/proof records. Independent source checks concentrated on theorem hypotheses, normalizations and proof-status boundaries. Each report record distinguishes full report-body reading from selected supplementary-paper passages.
corrections: Restricted Milman-Xu stability to the test fields supported by arXiv:2504.11185v1 Remark 1.4; did not infer stability for all physical variations from the informal overview.
Separated bubble count from cell count, spherical coning volume constants from area constants, and minimality from uniqueness ranges.
Added absolute continuity to the equal-mass statement for rotation-invariant measures, excluding atomic mass on the partition hyperplanes.
Retained the full invariant subspace in the mean ergodic theorem and the ergodicity hypotheses needed to identify limits as constants or zero.

Kept discrete positive-sign Fourier transforms separate from the site's Euclidean negative-sign convention; used the formal Weyl statement rather than the inconsistent radius in the source's explanatory prose.
Distinguished the point-evaluation constant C_p from the functional norm C_p^(1/p), and proved p=1 uniqueness without an incorrect appeal to strict convexity.
Split the Fourier problem's unrelated open questions into separate notes; justified the tempered-distribution interpretation for p<1 using the point-evaluation bound and translation invariance.
Made Paley-Wiener and sinc prerequisites explicit and defined the conjugate-reflection notation locally in the nonlinear reproduction proof.

limitations: The report records list deferred proofs and branches. A page with a local deduction from a cited theorem does not reproduce the cited theorem's proof.
Automated source, graph, formula and finite-example checks do not establish the mathematical correctness or complete prerequisite closure of all research results.
Banana Space terminology checks were access-limited; no claim of verified terminology equivalence is made.
Existing unrelated files and work were preserved. This request did not ask for a commit, push or public deployment.
